title: "AI Studio on Start + Void"
description: "AI Studio Worker identity, acceptance commands, smoke checks and Vercel rollback packet."
updatedAt: "2026-11-28"
audience: developers
---

AI Studio (`apps/ai`) runs on TanStack Start, Vite+ and Void with the shared
Start bridge. The native Worker owns `ai.tuturuuu.com`; no route or domain is
declared in source. Production publication remains held until exact-head CI,
sealed emitted-Worker acceptance, staging acceptance and rollback capture pass.
The existing Vercel deployment remains the rollback target until cutover.

## Cutover packet

| Item | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Production Worker | `tuturuuu-ai` (`VITE_AI_NATIVE_PROFILE=production`) |
| Staging Worker | the staging Worker name |
| Worker host admission | `ai.tuturuuu.com`, `ai.tutur3u.com`, and `tuturuuu.com/ai` for the production artifact. The release operator maps ingress separately. |
| Bindings | `ASSETS` (`dist/client`), `TUTURUUU_NOINDEX=1` in the source config; production artifact policy must be checked in its emitted config |
| Secret names | `TUTURUUU_APP_COORDINATION_SECRET`, `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`; provider credentials are optional: `GOOGLE_GENERATIVE_AI_API_KEY` or `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, `AI_GATEWAY_API_KEY` or `VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN` |
| Build | `VITE_AI_NATIVE_PROFILE=production bun run --cwd apps/ai build:cloudflare` |
| Prior Vercel deployment | No immutable deployment ID is recorded in the repository. Rex must capture the active AI Vercel deployment ID and URL before cutover. |
| Data | No database writes or migrations are part of this cutover. |

The AI Worker requires the coordination and Supabase secrets at startup. The
build logs only the selected provider category, never credential values.

## Acceptance and smoke

The `ai-cloudflare.yaml` cutover jobs run the emitted Worker checks before
upload and repeat them from a fresh restore. The production fixture checks
mounted asset caching and preserves the upstream WebGL sandbox while denying
framing on adjacent paths.

The emitted Worker verifies `/`, `/models`, `/v1/models` and `/api/build-info`
on both admitted root hosts and on the production apex mount. It also fetches
the rendered error document's assets on each variant. For private smoke, pin
the candidate at an operator-provided ingress that preserves the intended Host
and path. Record the Host and build-info source for each request so the smoke
proves the native Worker handled it.

Run the production build and emitted suite from the repository root:

```bash
export VITE_AI_NATIVE_PROFILE=production
bun run --cwd apps/ai build:cloudflare
CI=true CI_SOURCE_SHA="$(git rev-parse HEAD)" bun run --cwd apps/ai test:runtime
```

After the release owner deploys the accepted artifact and attaches the host,
probe the canonical origin without credentials:

```bash
curl -sS -D - -o /dev/null https://ai.tuturuuu.com/
curl -sS https://ai.tuturuuu.com/api/build-info
curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://ai.tuturuuu.com/api/build-info
```

Confirm expected page/auth behavior, the exact accepted source SHA in build
info, and `x-tuturuuu-runtime: native`. Smoke both the canonical subdomain and
the `https://tuturuuu.com/ai` mount if that mount is admitted by the cutover.
This packet does not authorize routing or provider changes.

## Mount at tuturuuu.com/ai

The production artifact serves `ai.tuturuuu.com` at its root and
`tuturuuu.com/ai` under its base. The gateway mount is one change: `/ai,/ai/*`
in `GATEWAY_MOUNTED_PATHS`, the `MOUNT_AI` binding to `tuturuuu-ai`, and `/ai`
in `PENDING_WEB_MOUNTS`.

| Request on `tuturuuu.com` | Served by |
| --- | --- |
| `/ai`, `/ai/en`, `/ai/vi` without a session cookie | AI Studio answers `307` to the AI product page (`/products/ai`, or `/vi/products/ai`), keeping the query |
| Other `/ai/...` pages | AI Studio with Web's shared session; a signed-out visitor goes to `/login` and returns through `/ai/verify-token` |
| `/ai/v1/...` | AI Studio's key-authenticated public API, including streaming |
| `/ai/api/...`, `/ai/_serverFn/...`, `/ai/assets/...` | AI Studio |
| `/ai/chats/...` | Web (publicly shared chats), listed in `apps/gateway/src/mount-web-paths.ts` |
| `/products/ai`, `/vi/ai`, `/en/ai`, `/api/...` | Web, outside the mount |

The documented public API base stays `https://ai.tuturuuu.com/v1`. The
Playground calls the API and its saved-key routes on the origin and base that
serve the page (`apps/ai/src/lib/playground-api.ts`): the apex mount cannot
call the subdomain cross-origin, and an unprefixed `/api` path there reaches
Web. A mounted app refuses `/api/auth/verify-app-token` and
`/api/auth/refresh-app-session` with `409`; it never mints an app session.

### Activation order

A committed mount is not held back by any later step. The `gateway` job of
`web-opennext.yaml` runs on a `production` push that touches `apps/web`,
`apps/gateway` or `packages`, merges every committed mount into the live
config, and moves traffic when `GATEWAY_CF_VERSION_UPLOAD_LIVE` is `true`. A
manual gateway publish from a commit that has the entry does the same. Land the
mount change on `main` only when all of these hold:

1. `tuturuuu-ai` serves, at 100%, a production-profile build
   (`VITE_AI_NATIVE_PROFILE=production`) of a commit with this mount support.
   Without a mount-capable build, `/ai` can answer `404` or call the Playground
   cross-origin; without the Worker, the gateway upload fails and blocks every
   gateway release.
2. The live gateway version and the current `tuturuuu-ai` deployment are
   captured for rollback.
3. No workspace uses the handle `ai` or `chats` in a way that the mount or the
   Web carve-out would shadow.
4. The gateway write is acknowledged for the exact commit.

After the write, capture the live gateway version and run
`node scripts/active-app-mounts.mjs --live <version.json>`. While `/ai` is in
`PENDING_WEB_MOUNTS`, Web keeps linking to `ai.tuturuuu.com`. Until Web
lists `ai`, a login that starts on the mount does not return there: Web treats
`/ai/verify-token` as its own callback and continues to the `nextUrl` path
without the base. Test signed-in pages with an existing `tuturuuu.com` session,
then remove `/ai` from `PENDING_WEB_MOUNTS` in its own change, rebuild the Web
families and repeat the signed-out round trip.

No automatic or manual publisher in the repository publishes `tuturuuu-ai`:
`ai-cloudflare.yaml` builds and seals both profiles without deploying, and the
`ai` recipe in `wave1-native-profiles.json` has no workflow that runs it. Step 1
needs a qualified publisher first.

### Mounted smoke

- `/ai?utm=a&utm=b` signed out: `307` to `/products/ai?utm=a&utm=b`;
  `/ai/vi` goes to `/vi/products/ai`.
- `/ai/personal/playground` signed out: `307` to `/login` with a `returnUrl`
  of `https://tuturuuu.com/ai/verify-token`.
- Signed in: `/ai` opens the app; a localized deep link with duplicate query
  keys keeps them; sign-out ends the shared session.
- `/ai/api/build-info`: `200`, `appName` `ai`, the accepted commit and
  `x-tuturuuu-runtime: native`.
- `/ai/v1/models` without a key: `401` JSON, never a Web redirect. With a test
  key, a streaming `/ai/v1/responses` call returns `text/event-stream` and a
  disconnect settles the run as `aborted`.
- Playground, manual key and saved key: model list and a run stay under
  `/ai/`.
- `/ai/chats/<public chat id>`, `/vi/ai`, and `/api/v1/ai/chats` still answer
  from Web (`x-gateway-family`, not `MOUNT`). `/products/ai` renders outside
  the AI mount (`x-gateway-cache` is not `MOUNT`; anonymous requests may be
  served by the `products` Marketing group or Web).
- Assets: run `python3 apps/gateway/scripts/mounted_assets_smoke.py --subdomain-url https://ai.tuturuuu.com/auth-error --apex-url https://tuturuuu.com/ai/auth-error --app-worker tuturuuu-ai --app-version "$AI_VERSION_UUID" --gateway-version "$GATEWAY_VERSION_UUID"`.

In CI, `mounted-login.runtime.mjs` checks the emitted production Worker's
signed-out root, login return, refused session minting and API paths on the
`https` apex, and `stream-cancellation.runtime.mjs` also streams through
`/ai/v1`. The signed-in round trip is covered by
`apps/ai/src/proxy-mounted-login.test.ts` with provider fixtures; confirm it
live.

### Mount rollback

For a full-cutover rollback, restore legacy routing and Web targets before
removing apex dispatch:

1. Pause gateway publication until live routing and committed config agree.
2. If the legacy-host redirect is active, reassign `ai.tuturuuu.com/*` back to
   `tuturuuu-ai` first.
3. If `/ai` has already left `PENDING_WEB_MOUNTS`, restore Web's legacy AI
   targets (`PENDING_WEB_MOUNTS` or the captured prior Web family version)
   before rolling the gateway back.
4. Roll `tuturuuu-gateway` back to the captured previous version ID
   (`cf workers deployments create --worker tuturuuu-gateway --strategy percentage --versions '[{"version_id":"<previous>","percentage":100}]'`).
5. Revert the mount commits before resuming gateway publication: the deploy
   helper keeps live mount paths and bindings, so reverting the source alone
   does not remove a live mount, and publishing the unreverted source adds it
   again.

The legacy-host redirect is a separate step. When `ai.tuturuuu.com` moves to
`tuturuuu-apex-redirect`, only browser navigations answer `301`
(`Cache-Control: no-store`). `/v1`, `/api`, `/assets`, `verify-token`, every
mutation and non-navigation fetches still reach `tuturuuu-ai`, so API keys,
SDK clients and Colab keep working.

## Rollback

Before switching, Rex records the active Vercel deployment ID, immutable URL,
and routing it serves. If smoke, authentication, error rate or latency regresses,
restore the captured host routing to that Vercel deployment in one step; do not
rebuild during rollback. Retain the Vercel deployment and routing until the
native Worker completes its stable release window.
